newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil aims to keep debt at 30 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil aims to keep debt at 30 pct of GDP.

text.p: The Brazilian government aims to keep its public sector debt stock at about 30 percent of gross domestic product and will try to pay off some 10 billion reais in "fiscal skeletons" this year, a newspaper reported Tuesday.

The Gazeta Mercantil financial daily, quoting Finance Ministry economic policy secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, said the government realized its efforts to rein in public spending had been derailed last year by unexpected one time expenditures. "Our objective is to keep the public sector debt at about 30 percent of GDP," Mendonca de Barros said.
He said an $8.0 billion recapitalization plan for state bank Banco do Brasil and a court settlement against the government of some $2.0 billion last year had been unexpected costs.
"We made an almighty effort but didn't advance an inch," Mendonca de Barros said.
The economic policy secretary said the government would start tackling this year a shortfall in a federal housing fund, the FCVS, which is estimated at some 50 billion reais.
"Don't be surprised if this number falls by half," he said.
Gazeta said some of the privatization receipts from state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD)
In order to identify other "skeletons" and drag them out of the closet, Brasilia has set up a Fiscal Monitoring Committee.
"No one knows yet the size of these liabilities but the idea is to pay off at least 10 billion reais this year," Gazeta said.
Mendonca de Barros said it would naturally cost money to retire the debts, but "we must eradicate this culture of thinking that everything ends up with the widow (the Treasury)."
